title: Normalized potential complexes and coefficient reduction
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $T$ a Noetherian excellent scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, and $\delta$ a dimension function [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Put $\Lambda_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ for $n\geq1$. For each $n$ let $K_n$ be a pinned potential dualizing complex for $(T,\delta,\Lambda_n)$ [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. Derived scalar reduction equips $K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{\Lambda_{n+1}}\Lambda_n$ with the reduced pinnings, and there is a pinning-preserving isomorphism $\rho_n:K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{\Lambda_{n+1}}\Lambda_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$ [def-kun-derived-tensor]. These comparisons are coherent for iterated coefficient reduction, and any family of pinning-preserving isomorphisms between two such systems intertwines the $\rho_n$. On Tate twists the scalar-reduction comparison is induced by $u\mapsto u^\ell$ on roots of unity.

If $f:T\to S$ is a separated finitely presented morphism of Noetherian excellent schemes with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-proper-morphism], use bounded constructible finite-Tor complexes and the finite-coefficient etale exceptional adjoints of compact support [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Their natural scalar-reduction comparison $(f_{n+1}^!M)\otimes^L_{\Lambda_{n+1}}\Lambda_n\cong f_n^!(M\otimes^L_{\Lambda_{n+1}}\Lambda_n)$ is an isomorphism. When $M$ is potential, this comparison respects the induced local pinnings and thus gives the comparisons $\rho_n$ for its extraordinary pullbacks.
